title: A debug console's command table
description:
Build the core of a debug console. A `Console` holds a table that maps command names to functions. Each command function receives the `Game` and one whole-number argument.

- `addCommand(name, fn)` registers a command. Registering a name again replaces the old function.
- `run(line)` takes a line such as `"gold 50"`: a name, one space, and a number. It calls the matching command and returns `true`. If there is no such command, or the line is not a name followed by a number, it changes nothing and returns `false`.

Commands are plain function pointers of type `void (*)(Game&, int)`.

```cpp
Console console;
console.addCommand("gold", &giveGold);
console.run("gold 50");      // true, gold is now 50
console.run("fly 1");        // false, nothing happens
```
hints: `m_commands[name] = fn;` both adds a new entry and replaces an existing one.

To split the line, put it in a `std::istringstream` (from `<sstream>`), which reads from a string exactly the way `std::cin` reads from the keyboard: `std::istringstream in{ line }; if (in >> name >> amount) { ... }`. If either read fails, the condition is false.
Look the name up with `find`. If it is found, call it: `found->second(m_game, amount);`.
